cards.explanation: The message tells the nations to go to battle against Edom, friends. The envoy says, “Rise up, and let us go to battle against her!” (Obadiah 1:1). The "her" is Edom. Getting a message from the LORD that starts with "Rise up" is not the kind of mail you leave unopened.

The pride of their heart is what the LORD says deceived Edom, friends. He says, “The pride of your heart has deceived you…” (Obadiah 1:3). Nobody else had to fool Edom, because its own heart did the job. When you're the one telling yourself the story, you're a very easy audience.

The answer is True, friends! The LORD says, “Though you soar like the eagle and make your nest among the stars, even from there I will bring you down…” (Obadiah 1:4). A nest among the stars doesn't change anything. The LORD says that even from there He will bring Edom down.

The answer is that they will be sought out, bakers. The LORD says, “But how Esau will be pillaged, his hidden treasures sought out!” (Obadiah 1:6). Thieves would steal only what they wanted, but this is different. Esau's hidden treasures get sought out.

The word is trap, friends. “Those who eat your bread will set a trap for you without your awareness of it.” (Obadiah 1:7). The trap comes without Edom's awareness of it. I think that's the part that stings.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says He will destroy the wise men of Edom and the men of understanding in the mountains of Esau (Obadiah 1:8). They don't save the mountains. Being the smartest ones in the room doesn't help when the LORD has spoken.

The answer is that they will be terrified, bakers. The LORD says, “Then your mighty men, O Teman, will be terrified…” (Obadiah 1:9). Terrified is the word for the mighty men of Teman. I'm just glad nobody asked me to be a mighty man.

The reason is the violence against their brother Jacob, friends. The LORD says, “Because of the violence against your brother Jacob, you will be covered with shame and cut off forever.” (Obadiah 1:10). The LORD calls Jacob Edom's brother. This is a heavy verse.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says, “On the day you stood aloof while strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gate and cast lots for Jerusalem, you were just like one of them.” (Obadiah 1:11). Edom didn't have to carry anything off to be counted with them. Standing on the sidelines still put Edom in that crowd.

The word is rejoice, bakers. The LORD says, “But you should not gloat in that day, your brother’s day of misfortune, nor rejoice over the people of Judah in the day of their destruction…” (Obadiah 1:12). Judah's hard day was no day for cheering. A neighbor's worst day isn't a party.

The answer is loot their wealth, friends. The LORD says Edom should not “…loot their wealth in the day of their disaster.” (Obadiah 1:13). Looting is one of the things on His list. Taking advantage of somebody's worst day is the whole problem.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says, “Nor should you stand at the crossroads to cut off their fugitives…” (Obadiah 1:14). The fugitives are from the people of Judah, and the crossroads is where Edom should not be standing. The verse goes on to say Edom should not deliver up their survivors.

What they did will be done to them, bakers. The LORD says, “As you have done, it will be done to you; your recompense will return upon your own head.” (Obadiah 1:15). Edom's actions come back around. Same measure, same direction.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says there will be deliverance on Mount Zion, and “…the house of Jacob will reclaim their possession.” (Obadiah 1:17). They get it back. That's good news after all those hard verses.

The word is stubble, friends. The LORD says, “but the house of Esau will be stubble—Jacob will set it ablaze and consume it.” (Obadiah 1:18). The house of Jacob is the fire, and the house of Esau is the stubble. That's the picture the LORD paints.

The kingdom belongs to the LORD, bakers. That's the last line of the whole vision: “And the kingdom will belong to the LORD.” (Obadiah 1:21). After the mountains, the fire and the list of lands, the final word is about whose kingdom it is. It's the LORD's.
